title: United States chemical-specific environmental concentration reference benchmarks
scope: Selected EPA National Ambient Air Quality Standards and public drinking-water Maximum Contaminant Levels; context for exposure research, NOT emissions and not company ratings.
distinctions: Emission or waste transfer mass (lb/year) is not ambient concentration (ppb, µg/m³) or a measured personal dose.
Air NAAQS and public-water MCLs regulate different media, exposure models, populations, and statistical periods; never sort these values together by purported chemical hazard.
NAAQS have required design-value statistical forms; a single monitoring reading is not by itself a compliance determination.

Drinking-water MCLs are enforceable public-water-system limits, not automatically coal-ash groundwater protection standards. CCR assessments require unit-specific background, wells and regulatory methods.
A smaller regulatory number is NOT a quantitative claim that the chemical is more toxic than another compound.
EPA RSEI is a chronic-human-health screening method, not a validated acute poison, ecological, odor or legal-culpability model.
